$comment: Members of the NativeScript surface this package models that read `undefined` until
something writes them. Held by scripts/check-nativescript-ns-defaults.mjs against
packages/nativescript-bridge/adwaita/src/ns-core.d.ts (the ambient slice) and
packages/nativescript-bridge/adwaita/src/testing/ns-core.mts (the off-device double).
MEASURED, NOT READ OFF THE TYPES. @nativescript/core's own .d.ts spells every one of
these as always-present, because `@nsProperty` generates the declaration from the class
field rather than from the `Property` that backs it. The measurement: each name below is
registered through `new Property({...})` with NO `defaultValue`, and `Property`'s getter
is `key in this ? this[key] : defaultValue` (ui/core/properties/index.ts:303) — so before
the first write the member is absent and the getter hands back `undefined`. Reproduced by
registering classNameProperty's own options on a bare class and reading the member:
`typeof === 'undefined'`, and `.split` threw the exact TypeError a device threw.
WHY THE LIST EXISTS AT ALL. Declaring one of these `string` is not a cosmetic slip: it is
what let Adw.Clamp hand a classless child's `undefined` to `replaceClasses`, killing
Learn6502's Android port at startup on a real emulator. `gjsify tsc` held that call
correct, and the double answered `''` where a device answers `undefined`, so neither the
type checker nor 1400 tests could see it.
ADDING A MEMBER TO THE SLICE. Measure what NativeScript answers before the first write.
If the Property carries no defaultValue, add it here and declare it optional in both
files. There is no exemption bucket: a member that belongs here and is declared
always-present is the defect, not a style preference.
